title: Alphabet, Sounds & Basic Pronunciation
titleThai: ตัวอักษร เสียง และการออกเสียงพื้นฐาน
summary: อ่านตัวอักษร สะกดคำ และแยกเสียงที่ผู้เรียนไทยมักสับสน

lessons.title: Read new words with a sound-first method
lessons.objective: Read new words with a sound-first method
lessons.thaiExplanation: แยกตัวอักษร ชื่ออักษร และเสียงของอักษรให้ชัด เริ่มจากเสียงท้ายคำและคู่เสียง R/L, V/W, TH ก่อนใช้ IPA เท่าที่จำเป็น
lessons.grammarFocus: A letter has a name, but it can represent different sounds. Focus on the sound inside a real word.
lessons.readingContent: Listen to the final sound. The word work ends with /k/. The word live ends with /v/. Clear final sounds make your message easier to understand.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Hi, I am Ploy. That is P-L-O-Y. I work on a data team. Now listen to my family name: Sae-Lim. S-A-E, then L-I-M. Say it with me. Then say these three words and stop on the last sound: name, work, live.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Say: very, work, reliable, three. Then spell your name and one technical word.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write four short sentences about the sounds you want to improve.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: Listen to the final sound.
Can you spell your name?
Architecture has four syllables.
A letter has a name and a sound.
Say the new word one more time.
Please say your name slowly.
I can read new words with the sound method.
Listen to the final sound in each word.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: พูด, กล่าว
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Say the word again, a little slower.

questions.prompt: Which word ends with the /v/ sound?
questions.explanation: “live” ends with the /v/ sound. “work” ends with /k/, and both “write” and “light” end with /t/. Say each word slowly and hold the last sound so you can hear where it stops.

questions.prompt: How many syllables are in “model”?
questions.explanation: “model” has two syllables: mo-del. Count the vowel sounds you hear, not the letters you see — the word has five letters but only two beats.

questions.prompt: Which two words end with the same sound?
questions.explanation: “spell and tell” both end with the /l/ sound. work ends with /k/ and live with /v/; name ends with /m/ while say ends in a vowel; and read ends with /d/, not with the /r/ that starts letter.

questions.prompt: Can you ___ your name?
questions.explanation: “spell” means saying the letters one by one, which is what the question asks for. You read a word that is already written, and you listen to a sound somebody else makes.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the /r/ sound?
questions.explanation: “read” begins with /r/, the sound Thai learners most often replace with /l/. letter and listen both begin with /l/, and word begins with /w/.

title: Phonics & Word Reading
titleThai: โฟนิกส์และการอ่านคำ
summary: แบ่งพยางค์ อ่าน vowel patterns และเดาคำเทคนิคอย่างมีหลักการ

lessons.title: Break long technical words into readable chunks
lessons.objective: Break long technical words into readable chunks
lessons.thaiExplanation: ไม่ต้องจำกฎ phonics ทุกข้อ ให้มอง vowel pattern, prefix, suffix และแบ่งคำยาวเป็นพยางค์ก่อน
lessons.grammarFocus: Prefixes and suffixes give clues. Re-li-a-bil-i-ty becomes easier when you read it in chunks.
lessons.readingContent: First, find the vowels. Next, divide the word into chunks. Then, mark the stressed syllable. Finally, read the complete word.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Here is a long word: availability. Do not panic. Say it in chunks with me: a-vail-a-bil-i-ty. The stress falls on the fourth chunk, bil. Now try one more: reliability. Same ending, same stress. Once you hear the chunks, long words stop being frightening.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Break down and read: architecture, embedding, reliability, validation.
lessons.writingPrompt: Divide five technical words into syllables and mark the stressed part.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: คำเติมหน้า
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The prefix re- often means again.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: คำเติมท้าย
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The suffix -able changes the word form.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: การเน้นเสียง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Correct word stress makes speech clearer.

questions.prompt: Which is the best chunking for “reliability”?
questions.explanation: “re-li-a-bil-i-ty” breaks at every vowel sound, so each chunk can be said on its own. The other options cut across the sounds and leave pieces such as “iab” or “r” that you cannot pronounce.

questions.prompt: A suffix is added to the…
questions.explanation: A suffix goes on the end of a word: reliable + ity = reliability. A part added to the front is a prefix, as in re-read.

questions.prompt: Which part of “rewrite” is the prefix?
questions.explanation: “re” is the prefix, the part added to the front to mean again. write is the base word, and neither ite nor wri means anything on its own.

questions.prompt: Where does the stress fall in “availability”?
questions.explanation: The stress falls on bil: a-vail-a-BIL-i-ty. Words ending in -ity stress the syllable just before that ending, which is why reliability and security follow the same shape.

questions.prompt: A prefix changes a word by…
options: adding a part at the front
adding a part at the end
questions.explanation: A prefix works by adding a part at the front: un plus clear becomes unclear. A part added at the end is a suffix, and neither one removes letters from the base word.

title: Core Vocabulary & Chunks
titleThai: คำศัพท์แกนกลางและวลีพร้อมใช้
summary: เรียนคำเป็น collocation และ chunks พร้อมระบบทบทวนแบบเว้นระยะ

lessons.title: Use six high-frequency technical chunks in complete sentences
lessons.objective: Use six high-frequency technical chunks in complete sentences
lessons.thaiExplanation: จำคำพร้อมเสียง รูปคำ collocation และประโยคตัวอย่าง เช่น make a request, handle an error และ retrieve data
lessons.grammarFocus: A useful chunk is easier to retrieve than an isolated word. Learn “send a response,” not only “response.”
lessons.readingContent: The client makes a request. The API validates the input and sends a response. If the request fails, the system handles the error.
lessons.listeningTranscript: In today's standup, listen for the chunks, not the single words. The client makes a request. We validate it. Then we send a response. If something goes wrong, we handle the error and retrieve the log. Notice that make, send, handle and retrieve each keep their own partner.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain a simple API flow using make a request, send a response, and handle an error.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write one sentence for each chunk: retrieve data, deploy an application, evaluate the result.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: The client makes a request.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: การตอบกลับ
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The API sends a JSON response.
The service retrieves customer data.
We evaluate the result before release.

questions.prompt: Choose the natural collocation.
questions.explanation: English pairs the verb “make” with “request”: make a request. “Do”, “build” and “cook” are all real verbs, but no native speaker combines them with this noun — collocations have to be learned as pairs.

questions.prompt: The service ___ data from the database.
questions.explanation: “retrieves” means to get stored data back, which is what a service does with a database. “returns to” and “sends at” attach the wrong preposition, and “evaluations” is a noun where a verb is needed.

questions.prompt: Which verb goes with “an error”?
questions.explanation: English pairs handle with error: the system handles the error. You answer a question and build a service, but an error is something you handle or catch.

questions.prompt: The team will ___ the new model before release.
questions.explanation: “evaluate” means judging how well something works, which is what happens before a release. You retrieve stored data, request something from a service, and respond to a message.

questions.prompt: What does the system do when a request fails?
questions.explanation: “It handles the error.” The passage pairs an if-clause with its result: if the request fails, the system handles the error. Nothing there mentions deleting, resending or stopping.

title: Sentence Building
titleThai: การสร้างประโยค
summary: มองประธาน กริยา กรรม และส่วนเติมเต็มในประโยคจริง

lessons.title: Build accurate Subject + Verb + Object sentences
lessons.objective: Build accurate Subject + Verb + Object sentences
lessons.thaiExplanation: ทุกประโยคหลักต้องมองหาใครหรืออะไรเป็นประธาน และเกิดการกระทำหรือสถานะใด จากนั้นตรวจว่ากริยาต้องการกรรมหรือไม่
lessons.grammarFocus: Subject + Verb: The service runs. Subject + Verb + Object: The model generates text. Subject + be + adjective: The system is reliable.
lessons.readingContent: The client sends a request. The API validates the input. The model generates an answer. The response is useful.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Let me describe our service in three short patterns. The service runs. That is subject and verb. The model generates an answer. Subject, verb, object. The response is useful. Subject, be, adjective. Three patterns, and you can already describe most of a system.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Describe a four-step system. Start every sentence with a clear subject.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write four sentences about an AI application. Underline the subject and circle the main verb.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: The subject performs the action.
Every complete clause needs a verb.
Text is the object in “The model generates text.”

questions.prompt: Which sentence has Subject + Verb + Object?
questions.explanation: “The model generates text.” has all three parts: subject (the model), verb (generates), object (text). “The service runs.” stops at the verb, and the other two use be + complement rather than an object.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: “The system is reliable.” needs “is” to link the subject to the adjective. The first option has no verb, “reliability” is a noun instead of an adjective, and “System are” drops the article and breaks agreement.

questions.prompt: What is the object in “The API validates the input.”?
questions.explanation: “the input” is the object, the thing the verb acts on. The API is the subject doing the action, and validates is the verb that joins them.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is missing a verb?
questions.explanation: “The response useful.” has no verb at all. English needs be even where Thai does not, so the sentence has to read The response is useful.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is Subject + be + adjective?
questions.explanation: “The system is reliable.” ends with an adjective after be. The output is JSON. also uses be, but JSON is a noun, and the last two use an action verb instead.

title: Nouns, Pronouns & Articles
titleThai: คำนาม สรรพนาม และคำนำหน้านาม
summary: ใช้ a, an, the และคำนามนับได้/นับไม่ได้ในบริบทข้อมูลและโมเดล

lessons.title: Use nouns and articles accurately with AI vocabulary
lessons.objective: Use nouns and articles accurately with AI vocabulary
lessons.thaiExplanation: Data และ information มักเป็นคำนามนับไม่ได้ จึงใช้ some data, much information หรือ a piece of information
lessons.grammarFocus: Data และ information มักเป็นคำนามนับไม่ได้ จึงใช้ some data, much information หรือ a piece of information
lessons.readingContent: The model uses some data. It returns a piece of information.
lessons.listeningTranscript: A quick note from the data team. We collected a lot of data this week, and we found one useful piece of information in it. Remember, we never say informations, and we never say an information. If you need a number, say two pieces of information.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The model uses some data. It returns a piece of information.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The model uses some data. It returns a piece of information.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ข้อมูลสารสนเทศ
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The response contains useful information.
The system stores the raw data in one folder.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: จำนวน, ตัวเลข
vocabulary.exampleSentence: A large number of users joined the class today.
Give me an example of a correct input.
She joined the data team last year.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrase.
questions.explanation: “Information” is uncountable, so it takes no “a/an” and never adds “-s”. When you need to count it, use a unit word: a piece of information. Data behaves the same way.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct quantity phrase.
questions.explanation: “much information” is right because information is uncountable: it takes much rather than many, and it never adds -s. Use many only for things you can count, such as many examples.

questions.prompt: Which noun can you count?
questions.explanation: “example” is countable: one example, two examples. information, data and advice are uncountable in English, so they take no a/an and no plural ending even where Thai would count them.

questions.prompt: The model returned an answer. ___ was short.
questions.explanation: “It” replaces a thing, and an answer is a thing. He and She are for people, and They would need a plural noun such as answers.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We collected a lot of data.
We collected a lot of datas.
questions.explanation: “We collected a lot of data.” works because a lot of fits both countable and uncountable nouns. many data and a data treat data as countable, and datas is never correct.

title: Verb System
titleThai: ระบบคำกริยา
summary: เข้าใจ V1, V2, V3, V-ing, V-s และกริยาช่วยก่อนเรียน tense

lessons.title: Choose the correct verb form after auxiliaries
lessons.objective: Choose the correct verb form after auxiliaries
lessons.thaiExplanation: จำสูตรหลัก: Modal + V1, have + V3, be + V-ing และประธาน he/she/it ใช้ V-s ใน Present Simple
lessons.grammarFocus: จำสูตรหลัก: Modal + V1, have + V3, be + V-ing และประธาน he/she/it ใช้ V-s ใน Present Simple
lessons.readingContent: The service can process requests. The team has deployed the update.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Here is my update. The service can process about a thousand requests a minute. The team has finished the first test. Right now we are working on the second one. Listen to the verb after can, after has, and after are. Each one takes a different form.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The service can process requests. The team has deployed the update.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The service can process requests. The team has deployed the update.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: The service processes each request.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ต้องการ, จำเป็นต้อง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: You need to check the input first.
The model can run on one server.
I work on the data pipeline every morning.
We have finished the first test.

questions.prompt: The model can ___ text.
questions.explanation: After a modal such as can, the verb stays in its base form: can generate. The modal already carries the tense, so “generates”, “generated” and “generating” all add an ending that does not belong there.

questions.prompt: She ___ finished the first test.
questions.explanation: “has” is the form used with she, he and it: she has finished. have goes with I, you, we and they, and neither is nor was can carry a past participle here.

questions.prompt: The service ___ requests every second.
questions.explanation: “processes” adds -s because the subject the service is third person singular. Present Simple marks only that one form, which is why we process stays plain.

questions.prompt: Right now the team ___ on the second test.
questions.explanation: “is working” is be + V-ing, the form right now calls for. works would describe a routine rather than something happening at this moment.

questions.prompt: You ___ check the input first.
questions.explanation: “need to” takes to before the next verb. Unlike can or must, need is not a modal here, so it keeps the to-infinitive after it.

title: Essential Tenses
titleThai: กาลที่จำเป็น
summary: ใช้ present, past, perfect และ future กับสถานการณ์ทำงาน

lessons.title: Report current, past, completed, and future work
lessons.objective: Report current, past, completed, and future work
lessons.thaiExplanation: Present Simple ใช้กับระบบทำงานทั่วไป Past Simple ใช้กับเหตุการณ์จบแล้ว Present Perfect เชื่อมผลถึงปัจจุบัน
lessons.grammarFocus: Present Simple ใช้กับระบบทำงานทั่วไป Past Simple ใช้กับเหตุการณ์จบแล้ว Present Perfect เชื่อมผลถึงปัจจุบัน
lessons.readingContent: We deployed the service yesterday. The team has completed the evaluation. We will improve the pipeline.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Good morning. Here is where we are. We started this work last month. We deployed the new service yesterday. The team has already completed the evaluation, so the results are in. Next week we plan to improve the pipeline. Listen for the time words. They tell you the tense.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: We deployed the service yesterday. The team has completed the evaluation. We will improve the pipeline.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: We deployed the service yesterday. The team has completed the evaluation. We will improve the pipeline.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: นำระบบขึ้นใช้งาน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: We deployed the service yesterday.
The team started the project last month.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: แล้ว, เรียบร้อยแล้ว
vocabulary.exampleSentence: We have already fixed that problem.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: วางแผน, แผน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: We plan to release the update next week.
The report was finished yesterday.

questions.prompt: We ___ the service yesterday.
questions.explanation: “yesterday” marks a finished point in the past, so Past Simple “deployed” is the form to use. Present “deploy” contradicts the time marker, and “have deploy” and “will deployed” mix two structures together.

questions.prompt: The team ___ already completed the evaluation.
questions.explanation: “has” builds the Present Perfect together with completed. The word already sits between the auxiliary and the participle, which is a position did and was cannot fill.

questions.prompt: We ___ the pipeline next week.
questions.explanation: “will improve” is the future form, and next week fixes the time. will improved marks the tense twice, and the other two describe work already done.

questions.prompt: Which sentence links a past action to the situation now?
questions.explanation: “We have deployed the service.” is the Present Perfect, which connects a past action to its present result. The past simple version fixes the action in yesterday and says nothing about now.

questions.prompt: We started this work ___.
questions.explanation: “last month” is a finished time expression, and Past Simple takes it with no preposition at all. since would need a perfect tense, and the last two are not used in English.

title: Questions, Negatives & Modals
titleThai: คำถาม ปฏิเสธ และ Modal verbs
summary: ถามข้อมูล ขอความช่วยเหลือ และระบุข้อกำหนดในที่ประชุม

lessons.title: Ask clear technical questions and state requirements
lessons.objective: Ask clear technical questions and state requirements
lessons.thaiExplanation: Wh-question ใช้ question word + auxiliary + subject + verb ส่วน modal ตามด้วย V1 เสมอ
lessons.grammarFocus: Wh-question ใช้ question word + auxiliary + subject + verb ส่วน modal ตามด้วย V1 เสมอ
lessons.readingContent: What does this function return? Could you explain the architecture? The system must validate the input.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Before we start, I have three questions. What does this function return? Where do the logs go? And could you explain the retry rule? One more thing. The system must validate every input, so please do not skip that step. If anything is unclear, just ask.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: What does this function return? Could you explain the architecture? The system must validate the input.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: What does this function return? Could you explain the architecture? The system must validate the input.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ทำให้ชัดเจน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Could you clarify the requirement?
Ask a question if the requirement is not clear.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: คำตอบ, ตอบ
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Please answer the question in one sentence.
You should check the log before you ask.
The report must include the error message.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: “What does this function return?” follows the order question word + auxiliary + subject + verb. “does” carries the tense, which is why the main verb stays as “return” and not “returns”.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct negative.
options: The system does not validate the input.
The system not validate the input.
The system does not validates the input.
The system no validate the input.
questions.explanation: “The system does not validate the input.” uses does not plus the base verb. The auxiliary already carries the tense, so validates would mark it twice, and not cannot stand on its own.

questions.prompt: ___ you explain the retry rule?
questions.explanation: “Could” makes a polite request and is followed by the base verb. Do you explain would ask about a habit instead, and the last two do not fit explain in this pattern.

questions.prompt: Which sentence states a requirement?
options: The system must validate the input.
The system might validate the input.
The system could validate the input.
The system would validate the input.
questions.explanation: “The system must validate the input.” states an obligation with no exception. might and could describe possibility and would describes a hypothetical, so none of them makes a rule.

questions.prompt: “Where do the logs go?” asks about…
questions.explanation: Where asks about a place. Why asks for a reason, who asks about a person and when asks a time, so choosing the question word is really choosing what you need.

title: Description & Connection
titleThai: การบรรยายและเชื่อมความคิด
summary: เชื่อมลำดับ เหตุผล ผลลัพธ์ และการเปรียบเทียบ

lessons.title: Explain a process with sequence and cause-effect words
lessons.objective: Explain a process with sequence and cause-effect words
lessons.thaiExplanation: ใช้ first, next, then, finally สำหรับลำดับ because สำหรับเหตุผล และ therefore/as a result สำหรับผลลัพธ์
lessons.grammarFocus: ใช้ first, next, then, finally สำหรับลำดับ because สำหรับเหตุผล และ therefore/as a result สำหรับผลลัพธ์
lessons.readingContent: First, the system retrieves documents. Next, it ranks them. Finally, the model generates an answer.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Let me walk you through it. First, the system retrieves the documents. Next, it ranks them by score. Then it sends the top three to the model. Finally, the model writes the answer. We rank the documents because there is only room for three. Therefore, that step matters.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: First, the system retrieves documents. Next, it ranks them. Finally, the model generates an answer.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: First, the system retrieves documents. Next, it ranks them. Finally, the model generates an answer.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: The input was invalid; therefore, the request failed.
The test failed because the file was missing.
First, open the file. Then run the test.
Finally, we send the result to the user.
The main reason for the delay was a missing file.

questions.prompt: Which connector introduces a result?
questions.explanation: “therefore” introduces the result of what came before: The cache was empty; therefore the request was slow. “because” gives the reason instead, while “although” and “unless” set up a contrast and a condition.

questions.prompt: The test failed ___ the file was missing.
questions.explanation: “because” introduces the reason for the failure. therefore would introduce the result instead, finally marks a last step, and although sets up a contrast.

questions.prompt: Which word marks the last step?
questions.explanation: “Finally” marks the last step in a sequence. First opens it and Next moves it along, while Because is not a sequence word at all.

questions.prompt: Which sentence gives a result?
options: The request was slow because the cache was empty.
questions.explanation: “Therefore, the request was slow.” presents the outcome of what came before. The because sentence gives the reason instead, and the other two only state a fact or a step.

questions.prompt: In the passage, what happens after the system ranks the documents?
questions.explanation: “The model generates an answer.” comes last, after First retrieves and Next ranks. Following the sequence words is enough to answer without understanding every word.

title: Work & TOEIC Grammar
titleThai: ไวยากรณ์สำหรับงานและ TOEIC
summary: ใช้ passive voice, relative clauses, word forms และ conditionals ที่พบบ่อย

lessons.title: Recognize high-frequency workplace grammar patterns
lessons.objective: Recognize high-frequency workplace grammar patterns
lessons.thaiExplanation: Passive voice ใช้ be + V3 เมื่อต้องการเน้นสิ่งที่ถูกกระทำ เช่น The input is validated before processing.
lessons.grammarFocus: Passive voice ใช้ be + V3 เมื่อต้องการเน้นสิ่งที่ถูกกระทำ เช่น The input is validated before processing.
lessons.readingContent: The report was reviewed by the team. If the test passes, we will publish the release.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Attention, team. The report was reviewed on Monday, and the changes were approved this morning. All test accounts are required to be closed before Friday. The release will be published as soon as the last test passes. Notice how often the action is mentioned before the person.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The report was reviewed by the team. If the test passes, we will publish the release.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The report was reviewed by the team. If the test passes, we will publish the release.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ตรวจสอบความถูกต้อง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: All input is validated before processing.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ต้องการ, กำหนดให้ต้องมี
vocabulary.exampleSentence: All users are required to sign in.
The request was approved this morning.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ตารางเวลา, กำหนดเวลา
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The meeting is scheduled for Monday.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ว่าง, พร้อมใช้งาน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The report will be available after the review.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive sentence.
questions.explanation: “The input is validated.” uses the passive formula be + past participle, which keeps the focus on the input rather than on who checks it. “is validate” and “validating” use the wrong form, and “validates” is active.

questions.prompt: The report ___ by the team last week.
questions.explanation: “was reviewed” is the past passive, be plus past participle, and by the team names who did it. reviewed on its own would make the report the reviewer.

questions.prompt: All users ___ to sign in.
questions.explanation: “are required” puts the users on the receiving end of the rule. require would mean the users are the ones demanding something.

questions.prompt: If the test passes, we ___ the release.
questions.explanation: “will publish” is the result half of a first conditional: if plus present, then will plus the base verb. will published marks the tense twice.

questions.prompt: The meeting is ___ for Monday at ten.
questions.explanation: “scheduled” is the word for fixing a time. available describes a free slot, approved means agreed to, and validated means checked for correctness.

title: Reading
titleThai: การอ่าน
summary: อ่านตั้งแต่ข้อความสั้นจนถึง documentation, API reference และ technical paper แบบย่อ

lessons.title: Use skimming, scanning, context clues, and reference words in technical reading
lessons.objective: Use skimming, scanning, context clues, and reference words in technical reading
lessons.thaiExplanation: เริ่มจากมองหัวข้อ โครงสร้าง และคำซ้ำเพื่อหา main idea ก่อนอ่านรายละเอียด จากนั้น scan หาชื่อ field, status code และเงื่อนไขที่โจทย์ถาม
lessons.grammarFocus: เริ่มจากมองหัวข้อ โครงสร้าง และคำซ้ำเพื่อหา main idea ก่อนอ่านรายละเอียด จากนั้น scan หาชื่อ field, status code และเงื่อนไขที่โจทย์ถาม
lessons.readingContent: Read the endpoint summary first. Scan for the required field and the error response. The reference word “it” points to the request object.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Here is how I read API documents. I skim the summary first to get the topic and the purpose. Then I scan for one thing only, the required field or the error code. I do not read every word. And when I see the word it, I stop and ask what it points to.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: Read the endpoint summary first. Scan for the required field and the error response. The reference word “it” points to the request object.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: Read the endpoint summary first. Scan for the required field and the error response. The reference word “it” points to the request object.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: กวาดตาหาข้อมูลเฉพาะ
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Scan the API reference for the required field.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: อ่านผ่านๆ เอาใจความ
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Skim the passage before you read the questions.
The topic sentence tells you the main idea.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: รายละเอียด
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Check the supporting details in the second paragraph.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: จุดประสงค์
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The purpose of the email is to request a delay.

questions.prompt: Scanning is mainly used to…
questions.explanation: Scanning means moving your eyes quickly to find specific information, such as a field name or a status code. Reading for the general idea is skimming, and neither one requires translating every word.

questions.prompt: You need one error code from a long API page. What do you do?
questions.explanation: “Scan for it.” Scanning means going straight to one specific piece of information without reading the rest, which is all a single error code needs.

questions.prompt: What does skimming give you?
questions.explanation: Skimming gives you the general idea, the topic and the purpose, in one quick pass. Exact numbers come from scanning, and no reading technique produces a translation.

questions.prompt: A reference word such as “it” usually points to…
questions.explanation: It points back to a noun mentioned before it. Finding that noun is what keeps a long technical paragraph from falling apart halfway through.

questions.prompt: Which one is a supporting detail rather than a main idea?
options: The endpoint returns a 404 when the id is unknown.
This page explains the orders endpoint.
This guide is written for new developers.
questions.explanation: “The endpoint returns a 404 when the id is unknown.” is one specific case, which makes it a supporting detail. The other three describe what the whole document is about.

title: Listening
titleThai: การฟัง
summary: ฝึกฟังแบบไม่มีข้อความ ตอบ เปิด transcript ทำ dictation และ shadowing

lessons.title: Follow a listen-answer-transcript-shadow-summarize workflow
lessons.objective: Follow a listen-answer-transcript-shadow-summarize workflow
lessons.thaiExplanation: รอบแรกฟังเพื่อจับความหมายรวมโดยไม่เปิดข้อความ รอบสองตรวจคำตอบด้วย transcript แล้วพูดตามเป็น chunks ก่อนสรุปด้วยคำของตนเอง
lessons.grammarFocus: รอบแรกฟังเพื่อจับความหมายรวมโดยไม่เปิดข้อความ รอบสองตรวจคำตอบด้วย transcript แล้วพูดตามเป็น chunks ก่อนสรุปด้วยคำของตนเอง
lessons.readingContent: First, listen without the transcript. Next, check the key chunks. Then, shadow each sentence. Finally, summarize the message.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Let us do this in four rounds. Round one, just listen. No transcript. Round two, answer the questions. Round three, open the transcript, check what you missed, and repeat the difficult chunks after me. Round four, summarize the whole thing in your own words. If you did not catch something, guess first.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: First, listen without the transcript. Next, check the key chunks. Then, shadow each sentence. Finally, summarize the message.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: First, listen without the transcript. Next, check the key chunks. Then, shadow each sentence. Finally, summarize the message.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: พูดตามเสียงเกือบพร้อมกัน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Shadow the sentence at a comfortable speed.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: บทถอดเสียง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Check the transcript after the second listening.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: พูดซ้ำ, ทำซ้ำ
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Repeat the phrase until it sounds natural.
Summarize the main points in your own words.
Guess the meaning from the words around it.

questions.prompt: What should you do before opening the transcript?
questions.explanation: The first pass should be listen and answer. The transcript is for checking what you heard, so opening it early turns a listening exercise into a reading exercise and hides the words you actually missed.

questions.prompt: What does shadowing mean?
options: speaking along just after the audio
questions.explanation: Shadowing means speaking along just after the audio, copying its rhythm before you have time to translate. Reading a transcript aloud is a different exercise with no listening in it.

questions.prompt: You miss one word in a sentence. What comes first?
options: Guess it from the words around it.
Look it up in a dictionary.
questions.explanation: “Guess it from the words around it.” Real conversations do not pause, so guessing from context is the skill that transfers. The transcript can wait for the second pass.

questions.prompt: What is the last step of the workflow?
options: Summarize the message in your own words.
questions.explanation: “Summarize the message in your own words.” comes last, after listening, checking and shadowing. Producing your own version is what proves you understood rather than recognised.

questions.prompt: The written version of the audio is the ___.
questions.explanation: “transcript” is the written version of what is said. A summary is shorter than the original, a chunk is a small group of words, and shadowing is a speaking exercise.

title: Speaking
titleThai: การพูด
summary: พัฒนาจาก shadowing สู่การอธิบายกระบวนการและนำเสนอหัวข้อเทคนิค

lessons.title: Organize a technical explanation with Point, Reason, Example, and Result
lessons.objective: Organize a technical explanation with Point, Reason, Example, and Result
lessons.thaiExplanation: ใช้ PREP เป็นโครงช่วยคิด ไม่ต้องเลียนสำเนียงเจ้าของภาษา เป้าหมายคือพูดต่อเนื่องและให้ผู้ฟังตามความคิดได้
lessons.grammarFocus: ใช้ PREP เป็นโครงช่วยคิด ไม่ต้องเลียนสำเนียงเจ้าของภาษา เป้าหมายคือพูดต่อเนื่องและให้ผู้ฟังตามความคิดได้
lessons.readingContent: I prefer RAG because it can use external information. For example, it can retrieve company documents. As a result, the answer can be more relevant.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Here is my answer in four moves. My point is that we should use RAG. The reason is that our documents change every week. For example, last month the policy changed twice and the model still had the old version. As a result, the team stopped trusting the answers.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: I prefer RAG because it can use external information. For example, it can retrieve company documents. As a result, the answer can be more relevant.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: I prefer RAG because it can use external information. For example, it can retrieve company documents. As a result, the answer can be more relevant.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ความคล่องต่อเนื่อง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Short daily practice can improve fluency.
Explain the process in three steps.
Make your point in the first sentence.
As a result, the response time improved.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ฝึกฝน, การฝึก
vocabulary.exampleSentence: I practice speaking for ten minutes every day.

questions.prompt: Which phrase introduces an example?
questions.explanation: “For example” signals that a specific case is coming. “As a result” introduces a consequence, “My point is” states the main claim, and “In conclusion” closes the answer — in PREP they each mark a different step.

questions.prompt: In PREP, what comes first?
questions.explanation: PREP opens with your point, the claim itself, so the listener knows where the answer is going. The reason, the example and the result all support it afterwards.

questions.prompt: Which phrase introduces a result?
questions.explanation: “As a result” introduces the outcome. For example brings a case, The reason is gives the cause, and My point is opens the claim: four phrases, four different jobs.

questions.prompt: What does fluency mean here?
questions.explanation: Fluency is speaking without long pauses so the listener can follow your thinking. It has nothing to do with sounding like a native speaker or choosing rare words.

questions.prompt: Your answer is one sentence long. What is missing?
questions.explanation: “a reason and an example” are what turn a claim into an answer somebody can follow. Speed and accent add no content, and a rare word will not fill the gap either.

title: Writing
titleThai: การเขียน
summary: เขียน message, email, summary, technical explanation, bug report และ incident summary

lessons.title: Write a clear technical update with status, problem, cause, and next action
lessons.objective: Write a clear technical update with status, problem, cause, and next action
lessons.thaiExplanation: ให้แต่ละย่อหน้ามีหน้าที่ชัด เริ่มจากสถานะ ต่อด้วยปัญหาและสาเหตุ แล้วปิดด้วย next action ที่ตรวจสอบได้
lessons.grammarFocus: ให้แต่ละย่อหน้ามีหน้าที่ชัด เริ่มจากสถานะ ต่อด้วยปัญหาและสาเหตุ แล้วปิดด้วย next action ที่ตรวจสอบได้
lessons.readingContent: The API is complete. However, the integration test is failing because the seed data is incomplete. I will update the data and rerun the test.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Quick voice update on the integration. Status: the API is done. The issue is that the test suite is still failing. The cause is incomplete seed data, and that one is mine. The next action is also mine. I will update the data tonight and rerun the tests before standup tomorrow.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The API is complete. However, the integration test is failing because the seed data is incomplete. I will update the data and rerun the test.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The API is complete. However, the integration test is failing because the seed data is incomplete. I will update the data and rerun the test.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: Keep the status update clear and concise.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: อัปเดต, รายงานความคืบหน้า
vocabulary.exampleSentence: I send a short update every Friday.
Please report the issue with a screenshot.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: สาเหตุ, ทำให้เกิด
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The root cause was an expired key.
I suggest a small change to the config.

questions.prompt: Which sentence gives a next action?
options: I will update the data and rerun the test.
questions.explanation: “I will update the data and rerun the test.” names who does what next, so the reader can check whether it happened. The other three report status or cause, which is useful context but not an action.

questions.prompt: Which sentence states the cause?
questions.explanation: “The seed data is incomplete.” explains why the failure happened. The failing test is the symptom, the rerun is the next action, and the API line is status.

questions.prompt: Which opening is the most concise?
options: I wanted to write today to let you know that, as of now, the integration test seems to be failing.
Hello, I hope this message finds you well and that your week is going smoothly.
There is possibly maybe an issue somewhere in the tests, I think.
questions.explanation: “The integration test is failing.” says the whole thing in one line. The others delay the point with greetings or soften it with maybe and I think until the reader cannot tell what happened.

questions.prompt: A usable next action includes…
questions.explanation: A next action needs who does it and when, so anyone reading can check whether it happened. An apology and a log may both be useful, but neither can be followed up.

questions.prompt: I ___ a smaller change to the config.
questions.explanation: “suggest” introduces a proposal. issue and cause work as nouns here, and update would need something that already exists to be updated.

title: Workplace & Technical English
titleThai: ภาษาอังกฤษในที่ทำงานและงานเทคนิค
summary: ประชุม รายงานความคืบหน้า อธิบาย blocker review code และนำเสนอ architecture

lessons.title: Report progress, clarify requirements, and explain a blocker professionally
lessons.objective: Report progress, clarify requirements, and explain a blocker professionally
lessons.thaiExplanation: ใช้ประโยคตรงประเด็นและแยก fact ออกจาก assumption หาก requirement ไม่ชัดให้ถามยืนยันก่อนเสนอ estimate
lessons.grammarFocus: ใช้ประโยคตรงประเด็นและแยก fact ออกจาก assumption หาก requirement ไม่ชัดให้ถามยืนยันก่อนเสนอ estimate
lessons.readingContent: The implementation is complete, but deployment is blocked by a missing permission. Could you confirm who can approve the access request?
lessons.listeningTranscript: Hi, quick one about the deployment. Good progress this week. The implementation is complete. But I am blocked. I do not have permission to push to staging. Could you confirm who approves that access? Once it is approved, I estimate one more day, and we still meet the deadline.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The implementation is complete, but deployment is blocked by a missing permission. Could you confirm who can approve the access request?
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The implementation is complete, but deployment is blocked by a missing permission. Could you confirm who can approve the access request?

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: สิ่งที่ขัดขวางงาน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: I need to report one deployment blocker.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ความคืบหน้า
vocabulary.exampleSentence: We made good progress on the API this week.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: กำหนดส่งงาน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: We can still meet the deadline on Friday.
Please confirm the requirement before we start.
I will give an estimate after the review.

questions.prompt: Which question asks for clarification politely?
options: Could you confirm the expected output?
questions.explanation: “Could you confirm the expected output?” uses a modal question to ask for a fact without blaming anyone. “Fix this now.” is an order and “You are wrong.” is a judgement, so neither invites the information you need.

questions.prompt: What is a blocker?
options: something that stops your work until it is resolved
questions.explanation: A blocker is something that stops your work until it is resolved, such as a missing permission. Reporting one early is what gives the team time to clear it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence separates fact from assumption?
options: Deployment is blocked by a missing permission; I think Anna can approve it.
questions.explanation: “Deployment is blocked by a missing permission; I think Anna can approve it.” states what is known and marks the rest with I think. The others present a guess as a fact.

questions.prompt: The requirement is unclear. What comes before your estimate?
questions.explanation: “Confirm what is expected.” An estimate built on a guess is wrong for a reason nobody can see, so one clarifying question protects the whole schedule.

questions.prompt: We can still meet the ___.
questions.explanation: “deadline” is the date something is due, and English pairs it with meet. You make progress, clear a blocker and give an estimate.

title: TOEIC Listening & Reading
titleThai: TOEIC การฟังและการอ่าน
summary: ฝึก Parts 1–7 แบบจับเวลา พร้อมวิเคราะห์ distractor และจุดอ่อน

lessons.title: Choose a TOEIC strategy by part and manage time across Parts 1–7
lessons.objective: Choose a TOEIC strategy by part and manage time across Parts 1–7
lessons.thaiExplanation: Listening เน้นเดาคำถามและจับ paraphrase ส่วน Reading ให้กำหนดเวลา Part 5–6 เพื่อเหลือเวลาสำหรับ Part 7
lessons.grammarFocus: Listening เน้นเดาคำถามและจับ paraphrase ส่วน Reading ให้กำหนดเวลา Part 5–6 เพื่อเหลือเวลาสำหรับ Part 7
lessons.readingContent: The meeting has been postponed until Friday. All participants should review the revised agenda before then.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Attention, all staff. The quarterly meeting scheduled for Wednesday has been postponed until Friday at two o'clock. Everyone who plans to attend should review the revised agenda beforehand. A notice with the new room number will be sent to your colleagues this afternoon.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The meeting has been postponed until Friday. All participants should review the revised agenda before then.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The meeting has been postponed until Friday. All participants should review the revised agenda before then.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: เลื่อนออกไป
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The team postponed the meeting until Friday.
She will attend the training on Friday.
Listen to the announcement about the delayed flight.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: เพื่อนร่วมงาน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: A colleague from the sales team called this morning.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ประกาศแจ้ง, สังเกตเห็น
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The notice says the office will close early.

questions.prompt: The meeting has been ___ until Friday.
questions.explanation: “postponed” means moved to a later time, which is what “until Friday” signals. A meeting can be attended and an agenda can be reviewed, but neither verb explains a change of date, and files — not meetings — are attached.

questions.prompt: “All participants should review the agenda.” Who is that for?
questions.explanation: “everyone who plans to attend” is what participants means here. TOEIC constantly swaps one word for another that means the same thing, and that paraphrase is what you listen for.

questions.prompt: Which word means a person you work with?
questions.explanation: “colleague” is a person you work with. A participant attends an event, an agenda lists what will be discussed, and an announcement is the message itself.

questions.prompt: You are short of time in Part 7. What is the best move?
options: Read the questions first, then scan for the answers.
Read every passage from the start.
Answer at random and move on.
questions.explanation: “Read the questions first, then scan for the answers.” Knowing what to look for turns a long passage into a short search, which is the only way Part 7 fits the time.

questions.prompt: The meeting moved from Wednesday to Friday. It was ___.
questions.explanation: “postponed” means moved to a later time. A cancelled meeting would not happen at all, and announced only means it was made public.

title: TOEIC Speaking & Writing
titleThai: TOEIC การพูดและการเขียน
summary: เส้นทางเสริมสำหรับอ่านออกเสียง อธิบายภาพ ตอบคำถาม เขียนอีเมล และแสดงความคิดเห็น

lessons.title: Respond to a workplace speaking prompt and write a complete email response
lessons.objective: Respond to a workplace speaking prompt and write a complete email response
lessons.thaiExplanation: งานพูดต้องตอบตรงและมีรายละเอียดสนับสนุน งานเขียนอีเมลต้องตอบทุกข้อกำหนดพร้อม opening, body และ closing ที่เหมาะสม
lessons.grammarFocus: งานพูดต้องตอบตรงและมีรายละเอียดสนับสนุน งานเขียนอีเมลต้องตอบทุกข้อกำหนดพร้อม opening, body และ closing ที่เหมาะสม
lessons.readingContent: Thank you for your message. I can attend the workshop on Tuesday. Could you also confirm whether participants should bring a laptop?
lessons.listeningTranscript: Hi, this is Mark, returning your message about the workshop. Regarding your first question, yes, I can attend on Tuesday. I apologize for the slow reply. I was travelling last week. I have attached the draft agenda, and I would recommend that participants bring a laptop.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: Thank you for your message. I can attend the workshop on Tuesday. Could you also confirm whether participants should bring a laptop?
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: Thank you for your message. I can attend the workshop on Tuesday. Could you also confirm whether participants should bring a laptop?

vocabulary.exampleSentence: Please respond to every point in the email.
I apologize for the delay in my reply.
I have attached the report to this email.
I am writing regarding your request for a refund.
I recommend the second option because it is cheaper.

questions.prompt: A complete email response should…
questions.explanation: It should address every requested point. TOEIC writing is scored on task completion, so an answer that is fluent but misses one of the questions still loses marks.

questions.prompt: You are late replying to a customer. Which opening is best?
options: I apologize for the delay in my reply.
questions.explanation: “I apologize for the delay in my reply.” takes responsibility in a neutral, professional register. Blaming the reader or announcing your own mistake bluntly costs marks and goodwill.

questions.prompt: Which phrase names the topic of an email?
options: Regarding your request for a refund
questions.explanation: “Regarding your request for a refund” states the subject in the first line, so the reader knows what the message is about before the details start.

questions.prompt: The prompt asks two questions and you answer one. What happens?
options: You lose marks for task completion.
Nothing, if the English is correct.
questions.explanation: “You lose marks for task completion.” TOEIC writing is scored against the prompt, so a fluent answer that skips a requested point is still incomplete.

questions.prompt: Which sentence recommends something?
options: I would recommend bringing a laptop.
questions.explanation: “I would recommend bringing a laptop.” gives advice, softened by would. The others confirm, attach or thank, which are useful moves but not recommendations.

title: LLM Architecture
titleThai: สถาปัตยกรรม LLM
summary: นิยามองค์ประกอบและอธิบาย flow ของโมเดลด้วย noun phrases

lessons.title: Explain the main components of an LLM architecture
lessons.objective: Explain the main components of an LLM architecture
lessons.thaiExplanation: เชื่อมความรู้ AI กับภาษา: นิยาม component ด้วย “X is a component that…” และใช้ noun phrases เพื่ออธิบายหน้าที่
lessons.grammarFocus: A tokenizer converts text into tokens. The model processes those tokens through multiple layers. A decoder predicts the next token.
lessons.readingContent: First, the tokenizer converts the input into tokens. Next, the model processes the sequence. Finally, the decoder produces output tokens.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Let me explain what happens inside. Your sentence goes to the tokenizer, which cuts it into tokens. Those tokens travel through many layers. At each step the model predicts the next token, one at a time. Then the decoder turns those tokens back into text you can read.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Give a 60-second explanation of tokenizer, layers, and decoder.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write a 70-word explanation of an LLM architecture for a junior developer.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ตัวแปลงข้อความเป็นโทเคน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The tokenizer converts text into tokens.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ชั้นของโมเดล
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Each layer transforms the representation.
The model predicts the next token.

questions.prompt: What does a tokenizer do?
questions.explanation: “It converts text into tokens.” Tokens are the small pieces the model actually reads, so tokenizing happens before anything else. Storing passwords, deploying an API and ranking databases belong to other parts of a system.

A decoder is a component that produces output.
questions.explanation: “A decoder is a component that produces output.” follows the standard definition pattern: term + is + a/an + category + that + function. The other options drop the verb or the relative pronoun that pattern needs.

questions.prompt: What does the decoder produce?
questions.explanation: The decoder produces output tokens, which are turned back into readable text. Indexes, keys and training sets belong to other parts of the system.

questions.prompt: The model predicts the next token ___.
questions.explanation: It works one at a time, using everything before it to choose what comes next. That is why a long answer costs more than a short one.

lessons.writingPrompt: Create a prompt that extracts API errors into a JSON array.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive form.

questions.prompt: Which rule is safest?

Every user should be an admin.
questions.explanation: “Secrets must be stored outside source code.” keeps a key out of the repository, where it would stay in the history even after deletion. The other three describe exactly the practices a security review looks for.

questions.prompt: Use ___ for a mandatory security rule.
questions.explanation: “must” states an obligation with no exceptions, which is what a security rule needs. “might” and “could” express possibility and “would” a hypothetical, so all three leave the rule sounding optional.

questions.explanation: A rate limit caps too many requests in a short time, whether they come from a bug or an attack. Passwords, schemas and database speed are handled elsewhere.

questions.prompt: Where should an API key live?
options: in a secret store outside the repository
questions.explanation: It belongs in a secret store outside the repository. Anything committed stays in the history even after you delete it, which is why rotating a leaked key is the only real fix.

questions.explanation: “Each step adds time to the same response.” Latency is the sum of the lifecycle, so a slow step anywhere is a slow answer for the user.

lessons.listeningTranscript: Every token costs money and time. A long prompt increases both the bill and the latency, so remove what the model does not need. But there is a trade-off between cost and answer quality. Cut too much context and you pay again in wrong answers. Measure before you reduce.

The prompt was too short before.

questions.prompt: What comes before optimizing?
options: Measure the current cost and quality.
questions.explanation: “Measure the current cost and quality.” Without a baseline you cannot tell an improvement from a regression.

lessons.readingContent: The second prompt has a dependency on the first output.
lessons.listeningTranscript: A chain is simply steps in order. The first prompt extracts the facts. The second one checks them. The third one writes the summary. Each step passes its output to the next, so each step depends on the previous one. If step one is wrong, everything after it is wrong too.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The second prompt has a dependency on the first output.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The second prompt has a dependency on the first output.

Pass the output of the first prompt to the second one.
Run the steps in the right order.
Each step uses the output of the previous step.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: รวมเข้าด้วยกัน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Combine the results into one final answer.

questions.prompt: What does each step in a chain use?
options: the output of the previous step
questions.explanation: Each step uses the output of the previous step, which is exactly why the order cannot be changed freely.

questions.prompt: Step two needs step one, so step two has a ___ on it.
questions.explanation: “dependency” names that relationship, and the preposition is on: a dependency on the first output.

questions.prompt: Step one extracts the wrong facts. What about step three?
questions.explanation: “It is wrong too.” Errors travel forward through a chain, which is why the cheapest place to check is the earliest step.

questions.prompt: ___ step passes its output to the next one.
questions.explanation: “Each” goes straight before a singular noun. All and any would need of the and a plural noun after them.

questions.prompt: Why split one large prompt into a chain?
options: Each step can be checked on its own.
questions.explanation: “Each step can be checked on its own.” Splitting buys visibility, and it usually costs more tokens rather than fewer.

lessons.listeningTranscript: Here is the pipeline in plain words. The files are loaded from storage. The text is extracted from each document and cleaned. questions.prompt: The files ___ from the storage folder.

questions.prompt: Getting the text out of a PDF is called ___.

questions.explanation: “So an answer can be traced back to it.” Without the source you can show a user an answer but never prove where it came from.

questions.prompt: In what order does the pipeline work?
questions.explanation: The order is load, extract, clean, store. Every step needs what the one before it produced.

lessons.readingContent: Each chunk should preserve enough context for retrieval.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Chunk size is a balance. Split a document too small and each piece loses the context around it. Leave it too large and one short question returns half a chapter. We keep a small overlap between chunks so that a sentence is never cut in the middle.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: Each chunk should preserve enough context for retrieval.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: Each chunk should preserve enough context for retrieval.

Split the document into short sections.
A small chunk size gives more precise matches.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ส่วนที่ซ้อนทับกัน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: A small overlap keeps the meaning between two chunks.
Very short chunks can lose the context of the sentence.

questions.prompt: What is the risk of very small chunks?
options: They lose the context around them.
questions.explanation: “They lose the context around them.” A sentence with nothing around it can match a query perfectly and still not answer it.

questions.prompt: What is the risk of very large chunks?
options: One match returns far more text than the question needs.
questions.explanation: “One match returns far more text than the question needs.” You pay for that text in tokens, and the model has more to sift through for the same answer.

questions.prompt: The shared text between two neighbouring chunks is the ___.
questions.explanation: “overlap” is the repeated part that stops a sentence being cut in half at a chunk boundary.

questions.prompt: Each chunk should ___ enough context for retrieval.
questions.explanation: After the modal should, the verb stays in its base form: should preserve. The modal already carries the sense of obligation, so the verb after it never takes an ending.

questions.prompt: How do you choose a chunk size?
options: Use the largest the model allows.
Match it to the file size.
questions.explanation: “Test it against real questions.” The right size depends on your documents and your queries, which is why the number is measured rather than quoted.

lessons.readingContent: An embedding represents semantic meaning as a vector.

The model converts text into numbers.
Each chunk becomes a vector of numbers.
Sentences with a similar meaning sit close to each other.

questions.explanation: An embedding represents the meaning of the text as numbers, which is why it can match wording it has never literally seen.

options: The embedding matches meaning, not words.
questions.explanation: “The embedding matches meaning, not words.” That is the whole reason to embed rather than to search for keywords.

questions.explanation: “convert” is the verb for changing something into another form, and it takes into: convert text into numbers.

lessons.readingContent: The router sends each request to the appropriate model.
lessons.listeningTranscript: The router decides where each request goes. If the question is simple, it chooses the small, cheap model. If the request meets the harder condition, long context or code, it routes to the larger one. The rule is written down, so you can explain any decision afterwards.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The router sends each request to the appropriate model.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The router sends each request to the appropriate model.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: กำหนดเส้นทาง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The router sends each request to the appropriate model.
The router decides which model handles the request.
If the request meets this condition, send it to the small model.
Choose the cheaper model for simple questions.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ง่าย, ไม่ซับซ้อน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: Simple requests do not need the largest model.

questions.prompt: What does a router decide?
questions.explanation: The router decides which model handles the request, and it decides before any answer exists.

questions.prompt: A short, simple question arrives. Where should it go?
questions.explanation: “to the small, cheaper model.” Paying the top price for an easy question is the most common waste in a routed system.

questions.prompt: ___ the request is simple, send it to the small model.
questions.explanation: “If” introduces the condition that triggers the action. Unless would reverse it, and although would turn it into a contrast.

questions.prompt: A rule that must be true before an action happens is a ___.
questions.explanation: “condition” is the test itself. The route is where the request goes afterwards, and the decision is the act of choosing.

questions.prompt: Why write the routing rule down?
options: So any decision can be explained afterwards.
So the router needs no code.
questions.explanation: “So any decision can be explained afterwards.” When a user asks why their request got the cheap model, the written rule is the answer.

lessons.title: Explain API Automation clearly in English
lessons.objective: Explain API Automation clearly in English
lessons.thaiExplanation: บทนี้ฝึก Triggers, actions, events, and schedules แล้วนำไปสร้าง technical explanation ที่ตรวจสอบโครงสร้างได้
lessons.grammarFocus: บทนี้ฝึก Triggers, actions, events, and schedules แล้วนำไปสร้าง technical explanation ที่ตรวจสอบโครงสร้างได้
lessons.readingContent: A new event triggers the automation workflow.
lessons.listeningTranscript: An automation has three parts: a trigger, a condition, and an action. A new file event triggers the workflow. A daily job runs at midnight and removes the old records. And an automatic retry covers the short network problems, so nobody is woken up at three in the morning.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: A new event triggers the automation workflow.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: A new event triggers the automation workflow.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: ตัวกระตุ้น
vocabulary.exampleSentence: A new event triggers the automation workflow.
The workflow starts when a new file event arrives.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: รัน, ทำงาน
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The job runs every night at midnight.
A daily job removes the old records.
An automatic retry handles short network problems.

questions.prompt: What starts an automation?
questions.explanation: It is started by a trigger, whether that is an event, a schedule or a manual run. Everything else in the workflow happens after it.

questions.prompt: A new event ___ the workflow.
questions.explanation: “triggers” takes -s with the singular subject a new event, and here trigger is the verb rather than the noun.

questions.prompt: A job that runs once every day is a ___ job.
questions.explanation: “daily” says how often it runs. automatic says that nobody starts it by hand, which is a different idea altogether.

questions.prompt: Why add an automatic retry?
options: Short network problems clear by themselves.
It removes the need for logs.
questions.explanation: “Short network problems clear by themselves.” One retry absorbs the noise, so nobody is woken for something that was gone a second later.

questions.prompt: Which part of an automation is the action?
questions.explanation: “removing the old records” is the work being done. The file and the schedule are triggers, and the retry count is a setting.

lessons.readingContent: The recovery plan restores service after a failure.
lessons.listeningTranscript: Reliability is measured, not promised. We monitor the service every minute and watch the latency, not only whether it is up. When something breaks, the recovery plan restores service first and the incident report comes after. A reliable system fails in a way you have already planned for.
lessons.speakingPrompt: Explain this pattern in your own words: The recovery plan restores service after a failure.
lessons.writingPrompt: Write three new examples based on: The recovery plan restores service after a failure.

vocabulary.exampleSentence: The recovery plan restores service after a failure.
We reduced latency by caching the common answers.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: เหตุขัดข้อง
vocabulary.exampleSentence: The team wrote an incident report after the outage.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: เฝ้าติดตาม
vocabulary.exampleSentence: We monitor the service every minute.

vocabulary.thaiMeaning: เชื่อถือได้
vocabulary.exampleSentence: A reliable system fails in a predictable way.

questions.prompt: What does monitoring watch besides uptime?
questions.explanation: It watches latency too, because a service that answers in thirty seconds is up and still unusable.

questions.prompt: Something breaks in production. What comes first?
questions.explanation: “restoring service” comes first. The report matters, but it can be written once users are working again.

questions.prompt: A system you can depend on over time is ___.
questions.explanation: “reliable” means it behaves as expected over time. available describes only this moment, and monitored just means somebody is watching.

questions.prompt: The recovery plan ___ service after a failure.
questions.explanation: “restores” takes -s because the recovery plan is a singular subject. Decide the verb ending from the head noun plan, not from the words standing next to the verb.

questions.prompt: What does “fails in a predictable way” mean?
options: The failure mode was planned for.
questions.explanation: “The failure mode was planned for.” Reliability is not the absence of failure but knowing in advance what a failure will look like.
